item: SECURITY: basic_auth exemptions were matched against the Host-derived request.url.path, so any route was reachable unauthenticated via a chosen Host header; guard now matches the routed scope path
notes: Found by the pre-ship adversarial review of the backlog-8 callback exemption, which was about to add a SECOND exemption on the same broken match. Root cause in starlette 0.41.3 datastructures.URL(scope=...): it rebuilds the URL as f'{scheme}://{host_header}{path}' and re-parses it, so request.url.path is attacker-controlled while FastAPI's router keeps dispatching on scope['path']. A request with 'Host: h/health?' therefore read back as path '/health' and skipped auth entirely. Reproduced on a real uvicorn with MANAGER_APP_PASSWORD set, raw sockets, no credentials: GET /api/channels -> 401 baseline but 200 [] with the spoofed Host, and GET /api/settings -> 200 with the full settings payload. item: SECURITY: contain the SPA fallback's file reads — the catch-all served any file reachable from _dist/<user path>, an unauthenticated arbitrary-file read whenever MANAGER_APP_PASSWORD is unset
notes: Backlog 16 described ONE primitive ('..' hops) and its canonical vector /%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd didn't even fire — wrong depth for the real dist. Reproduced properly on a real uvicorn with RAW SOCKETS (httpx normalizes 2 of 3 primitives away, which is how this class stayed hidden): 9 of 13 vectors leaked pre-fix, 0 of 13 post-fix. There are THREE primitives: (1) '..' hops, since uvicorn percent-decodes before routing, so /%2e%2e/x and /%2e%2e%2fx arrive as real parent hops; (2) an ABSOLUTE full_path — Path('dist')/'/etc/hosts' IS /etc/hosts because pathlib drops the left operand, so //etc/hosts escaped with no '..' at all, meaning the intuitive 'reject any ..' fix would have left it wide open (mutation-verified: that mutant is caught ONLY by the absolute-path checks); (3) a symlink inside dist pointing out. Fix resolves and contains instead of pattern-matching: _contained_file() requires is_relative_to(root) + is_file() + os.access(R_OK), and returns None on OSError/ValueError/RuntimeError so the route falls through to index.html rather than 500ing — the guard wraps BOTH resolve() and is_file() because a 5000-char segment raises OSError from the stat() inside is_file(), which would have given an anonymous caller a 500 + traceback-sized log write per request (same class as backlog 8's out-of-int64 id). Also fixed: any index.html spelling now carries _NO_CACHE (resolving first widened the set of spellings reaching the cacheable branch).
